correctness.summary: The Bellman-Ford/SPFA-style relaxation pushes a node into the queue every time its distance improves, with no in-queue guard and a non-circular queue of size n, so qt can exceed n and q[qt++] writes past the stackalloc[n] buffer (stack out-of-bounds write / UB).
correctness.triggeringInput: Any graph where total relaxations exceed n. E.g. n=4 (queue size 4), s=0, t=3, with edges 0->1, 1->2, 2->3 and a residual/reverse path that re-relaxes nodes: pushing s plus repeated improvements of nodes 1,2,3 quickly drives qt past 4, overrunning q. Reverse residual edges carry negative cost (cost negated in MinCostFlowAddEdge), making re-relaxations and thus overflow easy.
correctness.rootCause: Line 25 allocates 'int* q = stackalloc int[n]' but line 36 does 'q[qt++] = vv' inside the relaxation with no inqueue[] dedup and no circular wrap (unlike Spfa in MinCostFlowCancelCycle which wraps with qt>=n => qt=0). A node can be enqueued many times, so the number of live queue entries is not bounded by n and qt overruns the buffer.
correctness.suggestedFix: Add an inqueue[] guard so each node is queued at most once at a time AND use a circular buffer with wrap-around (qt>=n => qt=0) sized for SPFA, or size the queue large enough for the worst-case number of relaxations; mirror the Spfa implementation in MinCostFlowCancelCycle.

perf.summary: Hoist the four per-iteration stackalloc buffers (parent, dist, parentEdge, q) out of the doubly-nested scaling/iteration loops.
perf.currentCost: Lines 20-25 allocate parent (4n), dist (8n), parentEdge (4n), q (4n) = ~20n bytes inside `for delta` x `for iter` — i.e. O(log(maxCap) * n) localloc emissions. Buffers are fully reset at line 23 each pass anyway, so the allocation itself buys nothing.
perf.proposedChange: Declare the four stackalloc buffers once, before the `for (int delta = ...)` loop. Retain the line-23 reset loop (dist=MaxValue, parent=-1) inside the inner loop; q is reset implicitly via qh=qt=0. parentEdge needs no reset because it is only read along chains where parent != -1.
perf.rationale: Single stack reservation instead of one per inner iteration; smaller, stable hot working set; lets Burst/JIT keep the base pointers in registers across iterations. Pure instruction-count and code-size reduction with identical behavior.
perf.risk: None. Every consumed element is reinitialized by the line-23 loop or by the BFS fill before being read. Stack frame size unchanged.

perf.summary: Hoist the loop-invariant `cap[e2] - flow[e2]` reload and avoid re-reading to[e2]/cost[e2] redundantly in the inner relaxation.
perf.currentCost: Inner BFS (lines 31-37) reads cap[e2], flow[e2], to[e2], cost[e2] each via separate indexed loads. The residual `cap[e2]-flow[e2]` is computed for the `< delta` guard then the same edge's to/cost are loaded again; dist[uu] is reloaded each edge though invariant across the inner for-loop.
perf.proposedChange: Cache `long du = dist[uu];` once per uu before the edge loop (line 31). It is invariant over e2 and removes a dependent 8-byte load per edge. Minor: compute residual into a local `int res = cap[e2]-flow[e2];` reused only by the guard (no second use here, so limited), but the dist[uu] hoist is the real win.
perf.rationale: dist[uu] is loop-invariant w.r.t. the edge iteration; hoisting it removes one memory load per edge in the hottest loop and shortens the dependency chain feeding `nd = du + cost[e2]`. Helps Burst vectorize/schedule the relaxation.
perf.risk: None: dist[uu] is not written inside the edge loop (only dist[vv] for vv != uu when nd<dist[vv]; vv==uu cannot improve since nd=dist[uu]+cost and a 0-cost self-loop would still not satisfy nd<dist[uu]). Self-loop with negative cost would be a pre-existing algorithmic concern, not introduced here.

perf.summary: The inner shortest-path is a BFS-order relaxation that can re-enqueue nodes via plain FIFO without a closed/settled check, giving worse-than-necessary bounds; using the existing PotentialDijkstra/SPFA with potentials would tighten cost per phase.
perf.currentCost: Lines 28-38 relax edges in FIFO order and push vv whenever dist improves, but there is no dedup/inqueue flag and no potential reweighting, so on graphs with varying costs a node can be pushed many times and q (sized n) can overflow on a single phase since qt is never wrapped (unlike Spfa in CancelCycle which wraps qh/qt). This is both a potential correctness bound issue and extra work.
perf.proposedChange: Either (a) reuse the module's PotentialDijkstra (Flow.cs:112) with maintained potentials for O(E log V) per phase and guaranteed non-negative reduced costs, or (b) at minimum add an inqueue flag and a circular q (qh/qt wrap like MinCostFlowSpfa) sized to n and cap re-enqueues, matching the proven pattern already in CancelCycle.
perf.rationale: A potentials-based Dijkstra gives a strictly better and more predictable per-phase bound than unbounded FIFO relaxation, and avoids the fixed-size q[n] overflow when more than n enqueues happen in one phase. Capacity scaling with Dijkstra+potentials is the standard, asymptotically tighter formulation.
perf.risk: This is the most invasive change and borders on algorithmic redesign rather than a micro-opt; it can alter the order of equal-cost augmentations (but not the returned totalCost for a correct min-cost-flow). Validate against existing tests. The q-overflow concern should be confirmed against the assumed input bounds before relying on it; if callers guarantee <= n distinct enqueues per phase, only the relaxation-count win remains.
